fields.meta_title: Task Automation Software You Build From a Prompt | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Describe a task your team repeats weekly. Emergent builds the task automation that runs it on time and logs each run in a database you own.
fields.h1: Build Task Automation for the Work Your Team Repeats
fields.hero_description: Describe the chores that fill your week: filing, chasing, copying, checking. Emergent builds task automation that runs each one on a trigger and writes down what happened.
fields.features_heading: What Comes With Each Task You Automate
fields.features_subheading: Each task gets a trigger, a rule and a person to answer to. Add the parts below as the job asks for them.
fields.feature_1:
Triggers on a schedule or an event

Run a task at 3:00 PM every Friday, on the first workday of the month, or the moment a row changes in another tool. One app can hold a dozen tasks, each on its own trigger.
fields.feature_2:
Rules written as plain sentences

Write the condition the way you would explain it to a new hire: anyone under 40 hours gets a nudge. Emergent turns it into logic you can read back and change by prompting.
fields.feature_3:
AI steps for reading and sorting

Read an attachment, decide what kind of document it is and pull out the fields you name. A step the model is unsure about pauses until someone on your team checks it.
fields.feature_4:
Messages to one person, not a channel

Send a Slack or email message to whoever owns the task, record attached. Reminders repeat on the interval you set, and anything still open escalates to a manager you name.
fields.feature_5:
A log of every task the app ran

Write each run to a database you own: what triggered it, what it changed and who acted on it. Filter by person or by week when someone asks why a task did not run last month.
fields.feature_6:
The code is yours to keep

Export the whole app to your GitHub repository, its tasks and database included. Keep editing by prompting, or give the code to an engineer when a task needs something custom.

fields.usecase_heading: Recurring Tasks Teams Hand Off First
fields.tab_content_1:
Client documents filed by the app, not by the front desk

Every file a client emails to Tallis Accounting's documents inbox is read before anyone opens it. Owen Pratt's W-2 is recognized and saved to his client folder under a standard name, and his checklist moves to 5 of 7 received. A file from an address the firm does not know waits for a person.
fields.tab_content_2:
Before a new hire's first day, every owner has a task

Signing the offer in Kestrel Dental Group's hiring tracker creates six setup tasks spread across four owners. Each one is dated back from the start date: payroll five days before, the laptop three days before. Whoever has not closed a task by its date gets a direct message each morning until it is done.
fields.tab_content_3:
Anyone short on hours is asked by name on Friday

At 3:00 PM on Friday, Fieldwork Studio's app compares each person's logged hours with the 40 they owe. Four people are under, and each gets a direct message showing their own total and the days with gaps. Anyone still short on Monday at 10:00 AM is listed for their team lead.
fields.tab_content_4:
The close checklist, rebuilt on the 1st with owners

On the 1st, Globex Logistics' month-end checklist starts fresh with 18 tasks, each assigned to an owner and due on a set workday. Bank reconciliation is due on workday 3. If a task is still open when its workday ends, Dana Kerr, the controller, gets a Slack message the next morning.

fields.howto_description: Pick one task before you start. By the last step it runs on its own trigger, and nobody has to remember it.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List the tasks your team repeats
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Write one task as a rule
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Name a person for every outcome
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Connect the tools the task touches
fields.howto_step_1_des: Ask each person to note every task they repeat for one week, with how long it took and how often it came up. Circle the ones that follow the same steps every time and never need anyone's opinion. Those are your candidates.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Describe a single task in a few sentences: what starts it, which record it reads and what counts as done. Include the exceptions people handle without thinking, like a client who sends documents from a spouse's email address.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Decide who receives the message when the task succeeds and who hears about it when it cannot finish. Messages to a shared channel are easy to ignore. Address each one to a single name, with a backup for the weeks that person is away.
fields.howto_step_4_des: List every system the task reads from or writes to, and check that each one has an API. Emergent connects the app to anything with an API. For a tool without one, a scheduled CSV export is a workable stopgap until that changes.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Decide what the AI may do alone
fields.howto_step_5_des: If a step reads or sorts documents, decide which results it can act on directly and which go to a person first. A misfiled tax form costs far more than the minute a reviewer spends confirming where it belongs.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Run it beside the manual process
fields.howto_step_6_des: For two weeks, let the app run while the person who owned the task keeps doing it by hand. Compare the two results every Friday. Each difference is either a bug in the rule or an exception nobody wrote down.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Once two weeks pass with no differences, stop doing the task by hand and tell the team where the run log lives. Then take the next candidate off the list from step one and start again at step two.

plan.angle: The top 10 is definitions (IBM, Workato, Unito, Teamwork) and tool roundups (Digital Project Manager, Reddit, Jotform): they say what task automation is and list apps, but never show one task automated end to end. This page wins by showing four unglamorous recurring tasks an ops lead actually owns (filing client documents from a shared inbox, new hire setup, chasing timesheets, the month-end close checklist), each with its trigger, its rule, the person it reaches and the row it leaves, plus an honest note on when Zapier, Make or n8n is the better fit.
tab_stories: Tallis Accounting's documents inbox receives a W-2 from client Dana Whitfield, the app reads it, files it in her folder and ticks her tax checklist to 5 of 7 received.

When Kestrel Dental Group marks a new hire as signed, the app creates six setup tasks for four owners, each due a set number of days before the March start date, and the payroll task is the one still open.
Every Friday at 3:00 PM, Fieldwork Studio's app compares each person's logged hours with 40 and sends each of the four people under it a direct message showing their own total.
On the first of the month, Globex Logistics' close checklist rebuilds itself with 18 tasks, owners and due workdays, and the bank reconciliation still open on workday 3 goes to the controller.
